q7.answer: The client does not keep its own copy of the key. R1 loads each secret into the in-process SecretCache at startup, and R2 swaps a changed entry in the same cache about every 5 minutes. R3 has each provider call read the current value with cache.get(name) at call time, so the next request after a swap uses the new key. A 401 or 403 triggers one out-of-band refresh, rate-limited to once per 60 seconds, to shorten that delay.

q8.answer: A6 checks it. For each pod and each secret, the latest 'secret loaded' or 'secret rotated' log line must show the same version id as the latest version in the store at check time. The check also requires a wait of one refresh interval plus a margin after the last store write, no old-image pod left in the cluster, and normal provider error rates. A7 then revokes one provider at a time, only when A6 passes for that key and A0 shows no consumer still on the old key. Non-pod consumers are confirmed by their owners, not by A6, and how that confirmation works is still open.

q9.answer: The order is: set store access and KMS keys (A1), then issue new keys at each provider (A3, after the A2 dev store), then write the new keys to the prod store (A4), then ship the image that reads from the store, drops the api_key lines from config/app.yaml and adds the CI guard in the same change (A5). After that come the A6 check, the A7 revocations one provider at a time, and the A8 rollback block, which must be in place before the first revocation. Provider rotation comes before the store copy because the store copy needs the new keys to exist first.

q10.answer: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and loads the sandbox keys from orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own identity. The A1 policy gives engineers read and write on dev only, so they never reach prod. Base URLs come from the non-secret per-environment config, and no key file is written to disk. Where a provider has no sandbox key, make run --offline skips the store and uses a local stub server with a fixed dummy key held in memory. This only holds after A2 is verified, since until then local runs still read the live keys in the committed file.

q11.answer: The instance does not start with partial keys. R1 treats 'not found' as fatal at once and does not retry it, so the instance logs an error naming the missing secret and the error type, with no values, and exits non-zero. Lines for the two secrets that did load may already be in the log. The pod never becomes ready, so the A5 rollout halts and the old pods keep serving.
